plan.title: UC inflamed vs control hallmark activity per sample
plan.analytical_narrative: The question asks for a per-sample pathway activity score and a hallmark activity heatmap that shows which pathways separate the ulcerative-colitis inflamed samples from the controls. The input is a single gene-symbol count matrix from Salmon (12,000 genes x 12 samples, counts.csv) plus a 12 x 2 sample table (metadata.csv) with one condition column, 6 inflamed vs 6 control, unpaired, one batch. This is a sample-scoring question, not a gene-level DE question, so the plan goes: (T1S1) sample structure QC on blind vst — PCA on the top 500 variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes and detected genes per sample, with sample_01 (library size ~4x below the median) kept and explicitly inspected rather than silently dropped, because DESeq2 size factors already down-weight depth; (T1S2) minimal low-count filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smallest group size) and median-of-ratios size factors, producing the vst matrix that every scoring step consumes — no pre-scaled counts; (T2S1) the core deliverable, GSVA hallmark scores per sample on the 50 MSigDB human hallmark sets, tested with limma under ~condition and BH-adjusted across the 50 sets, rendered as the requested clustered heatmap of hallmark activity across the 12 samples annotated by condition; (T2S2) UCell rank-based scores on the same hallmark sets as an independent, sample-set-independent check, because a GSVA score of one sample shifts when the sample set changes and a 12-sample cohort with one low-depth sample is exactly where that matters; (T3S1) PROGENy footprint pathway activity with decoupleR mlm as an orthogonal, mechanism-oriented per-sample readout that is a footprint rather than a membership score; (T1S3) the consolidated report. With n=6 per group the score-level tests have 10 residual degrees of freedom — enough to rank hallmarks, not enough to treat a single borderline BH-adjusted hallmark as established, and the report must say so. Heatmap ordering is descriptive: samples clustered on the score matrix will tend to split by condition by construction, so separation claims rest on the limma test on the scores, not on the picture.

GSVA per-sample hallmark scores plus UCell rank-based scores, limma on the score matrix
Pathway activity with decoupleR mlm on the PROGENy footprint model
Hallmark activity heatmap across the 12 samples with reproducibility record

steps.question: Which signalling pathways (TNFa/NFkB, JAK-STAT, TGFb and the rest of the PROGENy set) show a changed transcriptional footprint per sample in UC inflamed colon versus control, as an orthogonal readout to the hallmark scores?
steps.description: Compute per-sample signalling pathway activity on the T1S2 vst matrix with the decoupleR multivariate linear model (mlm) against the human PROGENy footprint model, using the top 500 responsive genes per pathway. This yields one activity value per pathway per sample. Test the activity matrix with limma under the same ~condition design and adjust with BH across the pathways. Plot the pathway-by-sample activity heatmap with the condition annotation bar, matching the layout of the T2S1 hallmark heatmap so the two can be read side by side. State explicitly that a PROGENy score is a transcriptional footprint of pathway activity, not the expression of the pathway's member genes, and that no topology-aware impact analysis is performed. The PROGENy model must be human. If no human footprint model is resolvable in this environment, report that clearly and do not substitute a non-human model or a membership-based enrichment presented as an activity.
steps.context: Hallmark scores are membership-based aggregates; PROGENy footprints answer a different question (is the pathway signalling engaged) and are the appropriate second per-sample pathway readout for UC colon, where TNFa/NFkB and JAK-STAT signalling are the expected axes. SPIA, the topology-aware tool of record, is not available in this environment.
acceptance_criteria: A pathway-by-sample PROGENy activity matrix written as CSV, with the number of model genes present in the filtered matrix per pathway
limma results with BH-adjusted p per pathway for inflamed vs control
A pathway activity heatmap annotated by condition, laid out to match the hallmark heatmap
The output states that the score is a footprint, not member-gene expression, and that no pathway topology is used
Human PROGENy model confirmed; absence reported rather than substituted
constraints: activity_method = mlm (decoupleR multivariate linear model)
footprint_model = human PROGENy
top_responsive_genes = 500
interpretation = footprint, not membership
No topology-based impact analysis is claimed — SPIA is absent from this environment
caveats: A PROGENy pathway can change activity with no change in its member genes' expression, and the reverse — do not reconcile it with the hallmark result by assuming they measure the same thing
With 12 samples the per-sample activity estimates are noisy; read the between-group contrast, not individual sample values

steps.name: Consolidated report and reproducibility record
steps.question: Which pathways separate UC inflamed from control colon across the hallmark and PROGENy per-sample scores, and how confident can a 6-vs-6 cohort with one low-depth sample make us?
steps.description: Assemble one report from T1S1, T2S1, T2S2 and T3S1: the QC summary including sample_01's library size and its position on the PCA; the hallmark activity heatmap as the headline figure; the ranked table of hallmarks by limma t-statistic with BH-adjusted p, annotated with whether GSVA and UCell agree; the PROGENy pathway activity heatmap and table; and a short statement of which pathways separate the groups and which are ambiguous. State the limits plainly: n=6 per group, 10 residual degrees of freedom on every score-level test, one sample at ~4x below median depth, set-level scores derived from a 12,000-gene matrix so hallmarks with few present member genes are unreliable, and heatmap clustering that is descriptive rather than inferential. Do not report a hallmark as separating the groups on clustering alone. Include a reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, any random seed used, and the version of the hallmark collection and the PROGENy model.
steps.context: The user asked a scoping question — which pathways separate treated from control — and a small cohort answers it as a ranking with uncertainty, not as a validated pathway list.
acceptance_criteria: Report contains the hallmark heatmap, the ranked hallmark table with BH-adjusted p and GSVA/UCell concordance, and the PROGENy heatmap and table
Explicit limitations section covering n=6 per group, sample_01's depth, and the descriptive nature of the clustering
Reproducibility record with sessionInfo, package versions, seed, hallmark collection version and PROGENy model version stored with the results
No pathway is described as separating the groups on the basis of the heatmap clustering alone
constraints: reproducibility_record = sessionInfo, seed, package versions, gene set collection version, footprint model version — stored with the results, not in a separate note
Every reported separation claim traces to a BH-adjusted score-level test, naming which method produced it
caveats: Two scoring methods over the same 50 sets are a stability check, not replication in an independent cohort
With 50 hallmarks and 12 samples, a BH-adjusted p just under 0.05 is a lead, not an established finding
